summary: Join our Prudential Supervision of Financial Institutions Training Course to master regulatory frameworks and improve your financial institution's governance.
lede: Regulatory reporting training for financial supervisors covers how to interpret institutional reports and data to identify prudential risks. Designed for onsite examiners, offsite surveillance analysts and other professionals involved in supervision, it develops practical skills in checking data quality, comparing trends, assessing capital, liquidity and asset quality, and using early-warning indicators and stress testing to prioritize supervisory action and write evidence-based findings.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals working across various financial supervisory roles who are expected to protect financial stability and make defensible supervisory judgments.
audience: Central bank and supervisory authority staff
Onsite examiners and offsite surveillance analysts
Compliance, risk, and internal audit professionals
Ministry of finance or treasury staff
modules: Understanding Regulatory Reporting and Supervisory Data
Asset Quality, Credit Risk, and Non-Performing Loans
Liquidity Risk, Funding Stability, and Contingency Planning
Governance, Internal Controls, and Risk Management
Market Risk and Interest Rate Risk
Operational Risk, Technology Risk, and Resilience
Stress Testing, Early Warning Indicators, and Forward-Looking Supervision
Supervisory Findings, Corrective Actions, and Enforcement
prerequisites: Participants are expected to have a foundational understanding of financial institutions and prior experience in a supervisory or regulatory role.
